original_value: Over a million journal articles had been shared on public Facebook pages by 2017, but little is known about who is sharing (posting links to) these papers and whether mention counts could be an impact indicator. This study classified users who had posted about 749 links on Facebook before October 2017 mentioning 500 medical and health‐related research articles, obtained using altmetric.com data. Most accounts (68%) belonged to groups, including online communities, journals, academic organizations, and societies. Of individual profiles, academics accounted for only 4%, but the largest group were health care professionals (16%). More than half (58%) of all Facebook accounts examined were not academic. The non‐academic dominance suggests that public Facebook posts linking to health‐related articles are mostly used to facilitate scientific knowledge flow between non‐academic professionals and the public. Therefore, Facebook mention counts may be a combined academic and non‐academic attention indicator in the health and medical domains.

result.paraphrase: By 2017, public Facebook pages had shared more than one million journal articles, yet it remained unclear who was posting links to these papers or whether mention counts could serve as an impact measure. Using altmetric.com data, this study categorized users who had posted 749 Facebook links before October 2017 to 500 medical and health-related research articles. Most accounts (68%) were group accounts, including online communities, journals, academic organizations, and societies. Among individual profiles, academics made up just 4%, while health care professionals were the largest segment at 16%. Overall, more than half (58%) of the Facebook accounts analyzed were non-academic. This predominance of non-academic users suggests that public Facebook posts linking to health-related articles mainly help move scientific knowledge between non-academic professionals and the public. As a result, Facebook mention counts may reflect both academic and non-academic attention in the health and medical fields.
